Fit the horseshoe (sparsity) lens

Source: R/lens_shrinkage.R
fit_horseshoe.Rd

Gaussian linear model with a horseshoe prior (Carvalho, Polson & Scott 2010) via bayesreg. Resolves only for a continuous (Gaussian, identity) response with at least one predictor; otherwise a lens-scope abstention().

Usage

fit_horseshoe(
  pass,
  lens_spec = NULL,
  n_iter = 2000L,
  n_burn = 1000L,
  n_chains = 4L
)

Arguments

pass

A koine_pass with a Gaussian (identity) family.

lens_spec

The lens's registry record; defaults to the horseshoe record.

n_iter, n_burn, n_chains

Sampler controls.

Value

A koine_fb_fit, or a koine_abstention.

References

Carvalho, Polson & Scott (2010). The horseshoe estimator for sparse signals. Biometrika 97(2):465-480.

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(60), x2 = rnorm(60))
d$y <- 1 + 0.8 * d$x1 + rnorm(60)
pass <- koine_pass(y ~ x1 + x2, d, gaussian())
fit_horseshoe(pass, n_iter = 1000L, n_burn = 500L, n_chains = 2L)
# }
